title: Texas high-school softball full-authority pilot research docket — NOT PUBLISHED
dataPolicy: Verified 2026–27 UIL softball district identities and clearly season-labelled 2025–26 historical team evidence. Research-only. No individual pages auto-published or approved by this file.
method: Exact match school name+conference+district+region to official UIL softball PDF. Primary school/UIL records for historical facts. Unresolved areas stay in gaps and must be closed for complete-first-publication acceptance. Current staff cannot be inferred from prior championship rosters. Expanded with primary-source historical UIL finals, official school schedule/current-season caveats, school staff spelling corroboration and known stale postseason notices on October 11, 2026. Every historical claim remains season-labelled and neither roster reprints nor inferred playing-field addresses are approved. October 11 independent primary-source award pass: 2026 UIL TGCA all-tournament groups for four champions, 2025 Shiner/Ganado honors, 2025 Katy district venue naming and official 2026 Ganado calendar venue naming. Venue recognition DOES NOT imply exact field parcel, admission, ADA, parking or current 2027 location. Third-party Amarillo team records explicitly not elevated to official school confirmations. October 11 coach role research: current school athletic websites identify named Shiner, Pearland and Katy softball head coaches as-of verification (not explicit Spring 2027 appointments), Ganado official faculty listings confirm James Harp employment but do not imply current role, and Amarillo school live feed confirms actual softball launch activity without reliable program foundation year. October 11 independent TEA/NCES physical campus crosswalk: Katy HS campus is in Fort Bend County (despite Katy ISD district association with Harris County), Shiner HS is a combined grades 7–12 campus and TEA vs NCES student counts are not identical, and Ganado, Pearland, Amarillo Highland Park each have exact state campus IDs and dated non-UIL enrollments. No student private data collected.

facts.claim: The 2026–27 UIL softball alignment lists Shiner in 2A District 29, Region IV, alongside Ganado, Flatonia, Danbury, Burton, Louise, Weimar and Moulton.
Shiner won the 2026 UIL 2A Division II championship; the championship archive names Shiner as champion.
The official 2025–26 state-team record names Jason Keller as head coach and lists Anastacia Rehak, Patrick Walker and Kailey Moeller as assistants.
The Shiner official 2025–26 state-team profile lists fifteen state-tournament appearances from 1996 through 2026, including championships marked in prior years.

Shiner ISD's 2026 softball PDF published home-and-away opponents, varsity and JV distinctions, practices/scrimmages and a school contact line; it is a historical 2026 schedule, not proof of a released spring 2027 schedule.
The 2026 title game against Sundown finished 5–2; a contemporaneous recap describes Shiner avenging its narrow 2025 championship defeat.
The official UIL 2025–26 state-team page displays a 31–7 record in its tournament entry; do not silently substitute a third-party 22–7 subset or call it the verified postfinal record.

UIL's 2025–26 Shiner state-team sheet identifies championship years 2001, 2002, 2008, 2011, 2015, 2016, 2024 and 2026 within 15 state-tournament appearances; the 2001 and 2002 title-game results have separate historical UIL final records.

UIL's historical 2001 softball championship archive records Shiner defeating Joaquin 2–0 in the 1A title game after a 2–1 semifinal over Brock, with extra-inning details preserved in the official bracket.
UIL's historical 2002 softball championship record shows Shiner winning the 1A championship over Bosqueville 11–1 in five innings after defeating Collinsville 10–0 in a five-inning semifinal.

UIL's Shiner 2016–17 state-team sheet identifies Steven Cerny as the coach with assistants John Hoelter and Ray Neal; these are verified historic staff roles, distinct from Jason Keller's 2025–26 tenure.
The UIL 2025 2A Division II final bracket identifies Sundown's 9–3 championship victory over Shiner on May 29, 2025, making Shiner a runner-up that season rather than the champion.

The UIL May 24, 2026 state-tournament pairings listed Shiner at 31–7 entering its Thursday May 28 final against Sundown; this shows the record's pre-title-game cutoff date, not a verified postfinal total.

UIL's all-time softball tournament archive confirms Shiner had 15 state-tournament appearances and eight championships through 2026, despite crossing 1A, 2A, and 2A-Division-II eras; records must retain their historical conference rather than retroactively assigning all titles to modern 2A.

The UIL May 31, 2026 all-tournament release credits Shiner with five 2A Division II honorees, including its championship game MVP Lauren Springfield; tournament awards are not interchangeable with full-season all-district or statewide TGCA awards.

UIL's 2025 all-tournament release records Shiner honorees even though Sundown defeated Shiner in the 2025 2A-DII title game; those distinctions belong to the 2025 season and must not be mislabelled as a team championship.

A Shiner local sports archive from the 2001–02 school year identifies David Goetz as Lady Comanches head coach, with Paula Lester as assistant, and reports an historic winning streak; corroborate with an original school/UIL coaching record before treating all ancillary streak totals as verified.

The Shiner ISD athletics softball page currently names Jason Keller with Anastacia Rehak, Patrick Walker and Kailey Moeller in its Lady Comanche program coaching group, consistent with the 2025–26 UIL tournament submission; this is a present website listing checked October 11, 2026, not a dated 2027 appointment letter.

TEA campus 143903001 identifies Shiner High School in Lavaca County as a 7th–12th grade campus with 309 students in its 2025 School Report Card sourced to 2024–25. This is not 309 high-school varsity athletes or the special UIL alignment enrollment. NCES shows 311 enrollment using its different count definition.

facts.claim: Ganado and Shiner are separate UIL 2A District 29 softball schools in the 2026–27 official alignment; Ganado is not in Shiner's football alignment by default.
Ganado won the 2025 and 2026 UIL 2A Division I softball titles; the UIL source lists 2025 and 2026 tournament appearances.
The 2025 Texas House enrolled resolution reports Ganado's first softball state championship, its unbeaten postseason and 5–4 final against Riesel.
The 2026 championship game against Bosqueville ended 5–2, the second state title in a row according to contemporaneous coverage.

UIL's 2025–26 team record identifies coach James Harp and assistant coaches Malina Andel, Matt Ervin and Shauna Hazlewood; treat these as 2026-season staff until a current 2027 directory confirms continuity.
UIL's 2025–26 state-team entry displays 33–2–1, a tournament-sheet record that should not be called a definitive after-final record without dated reconciliation.

Ganado ISD's schedules directory explicitly provides a 2025–26 Ganado softball schedule, while its other athletics listings distinguish baseball, football, track, basketball and volleyball; the dated 2026 softball source is historical, not the unreleased 2027 calendar.
The UIL May 24, 2026 championship pairings list Ganado at 33–2–1 against Bosqueville at 30–8–1 entering the 2A Division I final; the 33–2–1 record is a prefinal submitted tally.

Ganado High School's school-controlled 2025–26 athletics calendar explicitly schedules varsity softball senior night and JV home games at the named Ganado Softball Field, establishing a real school-used field identity, but not a street address or verified accessibility/entrance details.

The UIL May 31, 2026 softball all-tournament awards list five Ganado 2A Division I selections, led by MVP Saylor Bures; these are season-specific honors selected by the Texas Girls Coaches Association.
The UIL June 1, 2025 all-tournament list identifies Ganado's Kyla Stancik as 2025 2A-DI title-game MVP; this is a different season and honoree than Ganado's 2026 Saylor Bures MVP.

Ganado High's current faculty directory includes James Harp and Shauna Hazlewood as faculty and Joshua Ervin as athletics director. The 2025–26 UIL softball state-team sheet separately identifies James Harp as head coach and Shauna Hazlewood as an assistant, but the newer directory does not independently label either person as a 2027 softball coach.

Ganado ISD identifies Ganado High School at 501 West Devers and the separate district administration at 210 South 6th Street; neither address is source-labelled the varsity girls softball playing field, so use the campus address for school identity only.

Ganado ISD's own facility map page links stadium, high school gym and junior high gym facilities but provides no separately labelled softball field map or visitor entrance. The school event calendar verifies Ganado Softball Field's name without revealing an address.

TEA campus 120902001 is Ganado High School in Jackson County, 9th–12th grades, with 221 students in its 2025 school report card. Ganado ISD separately confirms the actual school campus at 501 West Devers; do not substitute the district headquarters at 210 South Sixth Street or presume it is the varsity softball field.

facts.claim: UIL's 2026–27 softball conference table lists Katy High School in Conference 6A, District 22, Region III, with eight other Katy-named campuses as district peers.
Katy High School won the 2026 UIL 6A Division II state title, defeating Forney 7–2 in the championship game.
Katy ISD's published post-championship recap reports the finished 2026 season at 39–5, with a 22-game winning streak and a reported 97th home run.
The older UIL tournament team submission lists 38–5 before the championship and enumerates four state appearances (2007, 2015, 2019, 2026); annotate the submission date when comparing records.
Katy ISD identifies 2015, 2019 and 2026 as its three 6A championship seasons.

The UIL 2025–26 state-team profile identifies head coach Meghan Brown VanEtta and assistants Brian Schmitt and Judy Whillock; Katy High's school directory carries the coach's current staff role under a different display spelling.

Katy High School's official campus athletic contact page gives 6331 Highway Blvd, Katy TX 77494 as its general campus address; this is not, by itself, evidence for the precise softball home-field entrance or spectator parking.

Katy's 2025–26 UIL submitted team sheet lists the Tigers' state appearances as 2007, 2015, 2019 and 2026, with title markers on 2015 and 2019; Katy ISD's June 1 report confirms 2026 as their third state championship.

The official February 7, 2025 Katy ISD athletics schedule calls Katy High's varsity softball venue 'KHS-Softball Field' and assigns multiple February 13–15 Katy home games there; this proves the named home venue in 2025, not a 2027 field policy or precise spectator entrance.

UIL's May 31, 2026 awards release lists six Katy softball selections to the Conference 6A Division II state all-tournament team, including championship-game MVP Haley Schmitt; the list is historical 2026 recognition, not a future team roster.

The Katy High School current athletics coaches directory identifies softball coach Megan Vanetta, while the separate faculty listing gives Megan Vanetta with a 'Science / Softball Head Coach' title. UIL's 2025–26 tournament sheet spells the previous season's head coach Meghan Brown VanEtta. Current school display spelling has priority for a present-tense school role, with the UIL archival form preserved only where discussing 2025–26.

Katy High's athletics directory identifies Judy Whillock as assistant athletic coordinator; the 2025–26 UIL tournament sheet lists her among softball assistants, but those are separately defined roles and do not alone establish her spring 2027 varsity-softball appointment.

Katy High School's exact Texas campus code is 101914001, and NCES records the physical 6331 Highway Boulevard school location in Fort Bend County with 3,543 students in 2024–25. Katy ISD has a Harris County district designation in some TEA reports, but that is not the Katy High campus county and must never be applied to its team page.

facts.claim: Pearland is listed in UIL's 2026–27 6A District 19, Region III alongside Pearland Dawson, Alvin and other schools; school and Dawson teams must not be conflated.
Pearland defeated Waco Midway 6–3 to win the 2026 UIL 6A Division I championship.
Pearland ISD describes the 2026 title as the program's fourth, joining its 1996, 2010 and 2023 state championships.
The school lists eight UIL softball state-tournament appearances through 2026, specifically 1995, 1996, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2016, 2023 and 2026.
Pearland High's own softball page identifies head coach Michele Hyden and varsity assistant Lori Romero, and separate JV assistants. The official UIL team sheet lists additional 2026 assistants.
The UIL 2025–26 state-team sheet displays 37–6; do not label that as a verified final postchampionship season total without checking updated school figures.
Pearland High School athletics lists its campus at 3775 South Main, Pearland TX 77581; it is a campus address, NOT independently verified softball-field coordinates.

Pearland High's own athletics calendar lists separate varsity softball and JV softball filters, providing a school-controlled schedule lookup that avoids dependence on third-party scoreboard databases; current 2027 fixtures still require an actually posted calendar entry.

Pearland's school-issued softball ticket page has May 2026 semifinal game listings and a potentially inconsistent 'Game 3' opponent label; treat the page as a historical ticket notice rather than a validated current fixture or 2027 stadium announcement.

Pearland High's athletic directions and general information identify the campus at 3775 South Main Street; the school's softball team's exact physical home diamond cannot be inferred from city park softball inventories, other venues, or the football stadium.

The current school athletics general-information page lists Michele Hyden as girls athletics coordinator, independently corroborating the spelling of the 2025–26 head softball coach in the official UIL team sheet.

UIL's May 31, 2026 tournament all-star selections list six Pearland softball honorees in the 6A Division I group, including championship-game MVP Madelyn Guzman; this award evidence is specific to the 2026 state event, not an endorsement of current varsity roster claims.

The Pearland High official women's softball page currently identifies Michele Hyden as head coach, Lori Romero as varsity assistant, Haley Jordan as JV1 assistant and Kaitlin Owens as JV2 assistant; the listing was reviewed October 11, 2026 without assuming each appointment will remain identical for the 2027 competition season.

Pearland High School's TEA campus 020908001 belongs to Pearland ISD in Brazoria County and serves grades 9–12. TEA's 2025 school report card lists 3,408 students for 2024–25; NCES has published a different historical 3,412 figure under another reporting definition, so attribute the exact TEA count and year.
